payload.claim: `estimated_lines: 43` with `estimate_measured: true` looks implausibly low for this spec's actual scope. The `bug` type ceiling is 1300 changed tokens (~325 changed lines at the repo's own ~4 tokens/line), and `estimate_measured: true` makes `driver.py check` price the estimate at face value rather than applying the usual overrun multiplier. The spec requires four elaborately-specified multi-task witness tests (criterion 1 needs four hand-built tasks each driving several `Ledger.record_findings`/`record_rebuttal` calls in exact orders, plus exact-order and exact-payload assertions; criterion 2 needs another four tasks), a rewrite of an existing test's docstring and body, new `_`-prefixed helpers, and a restructuring of `_finding_facts` to thread `has_answer`/`has_rebuttal_error` flags through `_facts_for_task` and to split rebuttal-fact derivation into two ordered passes. Prior commits touching exactly this file pair for comparably-shaped multi-task witness work (`SA-0337`, `6e601608`: 894 insertions/23 deletions across `migrate.py` + `test_record_migrate.py`; `SA-0340`, `6a7b339c`: 895 insertions/38 deletions) landed an order of magnitude past this spec's 43-line estimate, with less per-scenario complexity than criteria 1 and 2 combined here demand. A cell building these criteria exactly as written risks being blocked by the `size` gate partway through after already spending budget, and `budget_usd: 30` / `max_attempts: 3` leave little room to recover. The operator should re-check what the cited prototype measurement actually covered (in particular whether it included the test file) before funding, and consider whether `type: feature` (3000-token ceiling) is the more honest classification.
